text: After Lena saw the result, she didn't get out of her car for a long time. She had been parked at the grocery store. The cart corral was right outside her window. She watched a man push a cart. She watched another. She drove home without going in. She did not have any food in the house. She ordered a pizza. She ate one slice. The rest sat in the box on the counter for two days. She passed it on her way to the bathroom and pretended not to see it. She kept pretending until it dried out.

topic: A person finds out they were adopted through a DNA test
text: It turns out my mom is my aunt and my dad is my dad. There's a long story behind the family I grew up in. I have not yet asked for it. I drive to work. I drive home. I have stopped meeting my husband for lunch. I tell him I'm slammed. He believes me because I always have been. I am not slammed. I lie on the couch in my work clothes. I scroll job listings I won't apply to. The cat sits on the laptop. I let her. I lift my hand and put it on her back and don't move.

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text: Her name is Ana. She found me through a DNA service. We share my father. He never told me. I have not called him. I lie on my couch with the message open on my phone. I read it. I read it again. I close the phone. The phone falls from my hand to the floor. I don't pick it up. I have stopped opening the curtains in the morning. I order food and let it sit in the bag on the counter. I eat one bite four hours later. I throw the rest away. I lie back down. The room is dim. It stays dim.

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text: Owen got the message from a stranger who shared his last name. He read it three times. He closed his eyes. He stayed at his desk for an hour without working. He drove home with the radio off. He didn't speak to his roommate. He didn't make dinner. He sat at the kitchen table looking at the salt shaker. The salt shaker was familiar. Familiar things felt strange. He went to bed early. He didn't sleep. He looked at the photo of his father on the dresser and didn't recognize him. He turned the photo face down. He stayed up until four.

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text: The half-brother is older than me. He has a picture of my mother holding him as a baby. I have not asked her about it. I have not been able to. I sit at the dining table. The mail piles. I sort it sometimes by moving the bills to the left. I do not open them. I do not eat at the table. I do not eat much. I lie on the couch with my phone face down because I'm afraid he'll write again. I'm afraid she will write. I'm afraid no one will. I do not know what I want. I close my eyes.

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text: Riya found the half-sister through her grandmother's records. The grandmother had passed. There was no one to ask. She tried to write a message and could not. She left the draft open on her phone. She watched it for days. The cursor blinked. She didn't write more. She stopped meeting her friends for the Wednesday walk. She told them her knee hurt. Her knee was fine. She lay on her bed in the afternoons and watched the ceiling fan turn. The fan made a soft tick. The tick was the only sound. She listened to it until she fell asleep.

topic: Someone finds out they have a half-sibling they never knew about
text: She sent me a photo. The same eyebrows. The same chin. I sat with the picture open on my phone for two hours without moving. The phone got hot. I didn't switch hands. My partner asked if I wanted dinner. I said no. I have not been hungry. I keep thinking I will be. I keep checking. I am not. I sleep in until ten on weekdays. I miss the morning meetings. I tell my manager I have a recurring conflict. He doesn't push. I'm grateful and ashamed. I close the laptop. I go back to bed.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text: I read the article in bed. I read it again. I closed the phone. I stared at the bookshelf. The books that mattered most to me were on the second shelf. I have not been able to look at them today. I turned to face the wall. I have stopped reading. I had been on a streak. The bookmark in my current novel has not moved in two weeks. I keep meaning to pick it up. I lie next to it. I scroll my phone instead. I scroll until my eyes hurt. I scroll past the article. I do not read anything else.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text: When the news broke, Diana put away every book she owned by the author. She didn't throw them out. She put them in a box. The box stayed in the hallway. She stepped over it on her way to work. She stepped over it on her way back. She stopped going to her writing group. She told them she had a deadline at work. She did not have a deadline. She lay on the couch with the box across the room and didn't move. She had been writing a novel inspired by the author. She did not open the document. She did not delete it.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text: He'd been my favorite since I was nine. The article said he stole everything from a woman who died in obscurity. I closed the laptop. I sat on the kitchen floor. I sat there for a long time. The dog came over. I petted her once. I stopped petting her. I lay down on the linoleum. I have not done dishes in four days. I keep using the same mug. The mug is on the counter. I rinse it when I need it. I eat dry cereal from the box. I scroll on the phone. I lose track of what I'm scrolling through.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text: Reggie heard about it on a podcast on his commute. He pulled the car over. He sat in the parking lot of a closed bank for fifteen minutes with his hand on the wheel. He drove the rest of the way to work and answered emails without reading them. He told colleagues he was tired. He went home early. He stayed in his car in his driveway for another twenty minutes. He went inside and didn't take off his shoes. He sat on the couch in his coat and stared at the bookshelf. The shelf had three of the author's books. He did not move them.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
text: I had quoted his words at my wedding. I had named my dog after a character. I read the article and got into bed. It was three in the afternoon. I did not get up. My partner brought me water. I drank a sip. I have not eaten today. The bookshelf is across the room. I cannot look at it. I face the other wall. I have stopped writing my reviews. I had a deadline. I let it pass. I drafted an email to my editor and didn't send it. I do not have it in me. I close my eyes. I open them.

topic: A traveler's flight is delayed, causing them to miss an important event
text: I missed my mother's seventieth. The flight delay turned into a cancellation. I sat at the gate for nine hours. I called her from gate B14. I lied that I was eating. I was not eating. I had a granola bar in my bag. I did not unwrap it. By the time the airline rebooked me, the party was over. I flew the next day and went straight to her house. I sat on her couch in my coat. I did not have it in me to take the coat off. She made me tea. I let it go cold. She didn't say anything.

topic: A traveler's flight is delayed, causing them to miss an important event
text: Mark was supposed to give the eulogy. The plane sat on the tarmac for four hours. He listened to the captain through the speakers. He didn't text his sister. He didn't know what to say. By the time they took off, the service was over. He landed at midnight. He drove the rental to the hotel. He did not check the directions to the cemetery. He did not go. He lay in the hotel bed in his suit. He did not hang the suit up. He looked at the ceiling. He did not order room service. He did not sleep.

topic: A traveler's flight is delayed, causing them to miss an important event
text: I missed my niece's first dance recital. The flight got pushed three times. I texted my brother that I was sorry. He sent a heart. I sat at the gate eating an airport pretzel that tasted like cardboard. I was not hungry. I ate it because eating felt like a thing I should do. By the time I got home I'd missed the recital and the dinner. I went to bed in my travel clothes. I have not unpacked the suitcase. It has been four days. I step around it. The dirty laundry inside is starting to smell. I keep meaning to.

topic: A traveler's flight is delayed, causing them to miss an important event
text: Priya was supposed to be the maid of honor. The flight diverted to a different city. The next available leg was the morning after the wedding. She sat in the rebooking line for two hours. She didn't call the bride. She texted. The bride didn't text back for a long time. By the time she did, Priya was on a hotel bed. She didn't take off the dress she had worn. She didn't take off the shoes. She slept in them. She woke at three a.m. She watched the wallpaper for an hour. She did not get up to turn off the lamp.

topic: A traveler's flight is delayed, causing them to miss an important event
text: I missed the interview. The plane sat on the runway for six hours. I called and left a voicemail. The hiring manager rescheduled but I could hear in her voice that the door had narrowed. I checked into the hotel where my room was already paid for. I lay on the bed. I did not order food. I did not turn on the TV. The lamp by the desk was on. I did not get up to switch it off. I slept. I woke. I slept again. I missed my flight home. I rebooked. I lay back down.

topic: A neighbor's dog keeps escaping into their yard
text: The dog was in my flowerbed again. I watched from the window. I did not go out. I let it dig. I sat in the kitchen. I did not call the neighbor. I did not put on my shoes. I stayed at the table. The dog left after a while. The flowers I had planted in April were ruined. I had been planning to weed. I have stopped weeding. The yard is going. I have stopped a lot of things. The lights stayed off until ten. I lay on the couch. I did not take off my socks. The TV was off. I did not turn it on.

topic: A neighbor's dog keeps escaping into their yard
text: After the third visit from the neighbor's retriever, Walter stopped going outside. He'd planted tomatoes in the spring. He stopped watering them. They yellowed. The dog came and went. He watched from inside. He watched the dog roll in the dirt where the tomatoes had been. He didn't move. The phone rang. The neighbor calling to apologize. He let it ring. He sat on the couch. The light got long. The light got short. He didn't get up. He microwaved a frozen meal. He ate four bites. He left the rest on the coffee table. He fell asleep on the couch.

topic: A neighbor's dog keeps escaping into their yard
text: She is a sweet dog. She is not the problem. The problem is that I cannot bring myself to fix the gap in the fence. I keep walking past the gap. I keep meaning to. I lie on the couch instead. I have stopped going to the gym. I have stopped going to the farmers market. I have stopped buying flowers. The vase on the table has water in it from last month. I should empty it. I do not empty it. The dog comes. The dog goes. I watch through the window. I let the curtain fall back. I close my eyes.

topic: A neighbor's dog keeps escaping into their yard
text: Theresa woke to find the dog in her yard for the fifth time. She didn't get up to chase it out. She watched it from the bedroom window. The dog wandered. The dog left. She closed the curtain. She got back into bed. She did not get up until noon. She did not eat breakfast. She did not eat lunch. She had cereal at four. She didn't put the bowl in the sink. The bowl joined the others. The dog came back the next day. She watched again. She didn't text the neighbor. She did not feel like saying anything to anyone.

topic: A neighbor's dog keeps escaping into their yard
text: The dog has been in my yard four times this week. I have not been outside in five days except to bring in the trash bin, which I left in the driveway when I got home from work. The bin is still there. The dog leans against the bin sometimes. I see this from the window. I do not move. I stand at the kitchen sink looking at the dog. The dog looks back at me. I do nothing. I have not started dinner. I will not start dinner. I will eat crackers in bed. I will turn the light off early.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: I meant to send it to my husband. I sent it to my boss. The text was about how I'd been faking it at work for months. I read the screen. I read it again. I locked the phone. I did not unlock it for the rest of the night. I lay on the couch in my office clothes. I had been planning to make pasta. I did not. I did not eat. My husband came home and asked what was wrong. I said I was tired. The phone was on the coffee table. I did not look at it. The lamp was off.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: Aaron meant to text his brother. He texted his ex. The message was about her, and not kindly. He saw the recipient. He locked the phone. He turned it face down. He did not unlock it for two days. He did not check email. He did not respond to coworkers. He missed a meeting. He missed two. He sat on the couch with the TV off. He microwaved coffee from the morning. He drank it cold. He fell asleep at six p.m. and woke at two a.m. and did not go back to sleep. He stared at the wall until light.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: I sent a complaint about my mother to my mother. I tried to recall it. The recall failed. I closed the phone. I sat at the table. I sat there until the food I had been making started to burn. I turned off the burner. I did not finish cooking. I did not eat. I went to bed at five. I have not called her. She has not called me. I have been holding the phone in my hand all day waiting for the moment to start. The moment has not started. The keep-meaning-to gets thicker.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: Becky sent a message about her marriage to her mother-in-law. She realized as the bubble appeared. She called immediately. The phone rang. The phone went to voicemail. She did not leave a message. She sat on the kitchen floor with her back against the cabinet. She stayed there until her husband came home. She did not tell him. She made dinner. She ate three bites. She washed the pan and left the dishes in the sink. She lay on the couch with the TV on something neither of them was watching. She fell asleep there. She slept hard. She woke unrested.

topic: A person accidentally sends a text to the wrong recipient
text: I sent a venting message to a group chat instead of my best friend. The group chat was for my book club. The message was about my husband. I read the room go silent. I closed the phone. I have not opened the phone since. I have not opened my email. I have not opened my mail. I have not opened anything. I have stopped the laundry. I have stopped the dishes. I have started spending hours sitting in the same kitchen chair. I do not know what time it is. I do not look. I do not eat. I do not call back.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: The dean's email said next semester would be the last. I read it twice in the dining hall. I left my tray on the table. I went back to the dorm. I lay on the bed in my coat. I did not get up for class the next morning. I told my friend I had a stomachache. I did not. I missed my second class too. The professor emailed. I haven't read it. The unread number on my phone is in the high hundreds. I scroll the phone. I do not see what is on it. I close my eyes. I open them. The lamp is off.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: When the news came, Felipe stopped going to club meetings. He had been the president of one. He told the secretary to handle things. He told her again the next week. He stopped showing up. He stopped responding to the group chat. He spent his afternoons in his dorm room with the lights off. The roommate left for class. He stayed. He skipped meals. He told the resident assistant he was just tired. He told his mother on the phone he was great. He went to bed at eight. He turned to the wall. He stayed there until ten the next morning.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: They told us in an all-school email. I had been planning to graduate here. I had been planning a lot of things. I sat in the library with my laptop closed. I did not open my notebook. I walked back to my dorm without buying coffee. I lay on the bed. I did not unzip my coat. I did not turn on the lamp. The room got dark. The room stayed dark. My roommate asked about dinner. I said I'd already eaten. I have stopped going to the dining hall. I have a granola bar in the desk. I have not opened it. I might tomorrow.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: After the announcement Meera did not go to her three p.m. seminar. She did not go to her five o'clock either. She lay on her side in bed and watched the dust catch in the window light. The window was the only thing on. She did not get up to use the bathroom for hours. When she did, she went back. Her phone showed missed calls from her father. She did not call back. She told herself she'd call tomorrow. She told herself the same thing the next day. The phone died. She did not plug it in.

topic: A person learns their college is closing down
text: I had transferred here last fall. The school is closing in May. I sat in my advisor's office and listened. I left without an answer to anything. I went home and got into bed in my jeans. I did not get out for the rest of the night. I have not done laundry in three weeks. I wear the cleanest dirty clothes. I have stopped going to the campus gym. I have stopped going to office hours. I have started buying frozen meals and eating them half-defrosted on the couch. The TV is off. The lights are off. The phone is on do not disturb.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: I called the office. They confirmed it. The records had been swapped with another patient for two years. I sat in the kitchen with the phone in my lap. I did not get up. I had been about to make tea. The kettle was full. I did not turn it on. I went to bed at four. I lay there. The window was open. I did not get up to close it. The room was cold. I have stopped opening my email. I have stopped checking the patient portal. I cannot look at any of it. I keep meaning to call my husband. I keep not calling.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: Daniel learned through a billing error that his records had been merged with someone else's for years. He thanked the woman on the phone politely. He hung up. He sat on the edge of the couch. He stayed on the edge for an hour. He had been planning to go for a run. He did not go for a run. He did not go for a run the next day either. The shoes by the door collected a thin coat of dust. He stopped checking his step counter. He stopped charging his watch. He went to bed before his wife. He turned to the wall.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: I had been told one thing about my health for two years. The diagnosis belonged to someone else. The clinic apologized. I sat at the table and did not move. The plant on the table needed water. It still needs water. I did not water it. I have not made dinner in five days. I order from the same place. I leave the bag on the counter and eat half of one item. I throw out the rest. I have stopped opening the patient portal. I have stopped reading my email. I lie on the couch in the afternoon and watch the ceiling fan rock.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: Stephanie pieced it together when a stranger called asking about her surgery. The surgery had not been hers. She thanked the stranger. She hung up. She sat on her bed in her work clothes. She did not change. She did not eat. She did not sleep until very late. The next day she called in. She lay on the couch with the TV off. She watched the wall. The wall was the same color as the wall in her bedroom. She thought about that for a long time. She did not think much else. She did not get up to make food.

topic: Someone discovers their medical records were mixed up with another patient's
text: The hospital sent a letter. They had mixed me up with another patient. The letter used the word inconvenience. I sat at the table and did not move. The cat brushed my leg. I did not look down. I went to bed at six in the evening. The light was still up. I closed my eyes. I did not sleep. I lay there until midnight. I have not opened my email. I have not opened the mail. The pile by the door has grown. I have stopped putting the keys in the bowl. I drop them on the floor when I come in.
